questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option 1.Adolescence is defined as both a period and a process during which a child matures in terms of growth only.
2.The adolescence period typically spans from 12 to 18 years of age and serves as a bridge between childhood and adulthood.
3.Common causes for adolescents to start using drugs and alcohol include curiosity, a need for adventure, and experimentation.
4.Stress from academic pressures and the perception that using drugs or alcohol is "cool" are significant factors motivating adolescents to engage in these behaviors.
5.Media such as television, movies, and the internet, along with unstable family structures and peer pressure, contribute to drug and alcohol abuse among adolescents.
questions.solution: Adolescence means both ‘a period’ and ‘a process’ during which a child becomes mature in terms of his/her attitudes and beliefs for effective participation in society. The period between 12-18 years of age may be thought of as adolescence period. In other words, adolescence is a bridge linking childhood and adulthood. Adolescence is accompanied by several biological and behavioural changes. Adolescence, thus is a very vulnerable phase of mental and psychological development of an individual. Curiosity, need for adventure and excitement, and experimentation, constitute common causes, which motivate youngsters towards drug and alcohol use. A child’s natural curiosity motivates him/her to experiment. This is complicated further by effects that might be perceived as benefits, of alcohol or drug use. Thus, the first use of drugs or alcohol may be out of curiosity or experimentation, but later the child starts using these to escape facing problems. Of late, stress, from pressures to excel in academics or examinations, has played a significant role in persuading the youngsters to try alcohol and drugs. The perception among youth that it is ‘cool’ or progressive to smoke, use drugs or alcohol, is also in a way a major cause for youth to start these habits. Television, movies, newspapers, internet also help to promote this perception. Other factors that have been seen to be associated with drug and alcohol abuse among adolescents are unstable or unsupportive family structures and peer pressure.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option 1.The perceived benefits of drugs and alcohol, such as euphoria and temporary well-being, often lead to repeated use and addiction.
2.Addiction involves a psychological attachment to the effects of drugs and alcohol, driving people to use them even when not needed or when harmful.
3.With repeated use, the body's tolerance to drugs increases, requiring higher doses to achieve the same effect, leading to greater addiction.
4.Dependence on drugs and alcohol is characterized by withdrawal symptoms like anxiety, shakiness, nausea, and sweating if use is abruptly stopped.
5.Severe withdrawal symptoms may require medical supervision, and dependence often results in social adjustment problems as individuals prioritize obtaining substances over social norms.
questions.solution: Because of the perceived benefits, drugs are frequently used repeatedly. The most important thing, which one fails to realise, is the inherent addictive nature of alcohol and drugs. Addiction is a psychological attachment to certain effects –such as euphoria and a temporary feeling of well-being – associated with drugs and alcohol. These drive people to take them even when these are not needed, or even when their use becomes self-destructive. With repeated use of drugs, the tolerance level of the receptors present in our body increases. Consequently the receptors respond only to higher doses of drugs or alcohol leading to greater intake and addiction. However, it should be clearly borne in mind that use of these drugs even once, can be a fore-runner to addiction. Thus, the addictive potential of drugs and alcohol, pull the user into a vicious circle leading to their regular use (abuse) from which he/she may not be able to get out. In the absence of any guidance or counselling, the person gets addicted and becomes dependent on their use. Dependence is the tendency of the body to manifest a characteristic and unpleasant withdrawal syndrome if regular dose of drugs/alcohol is abruptly discontinued. This is characterised by anxiety, shakiness, nausea and sweating, which may be relieved when use is resumed again. In some cases, withdrawal symptoms can be severe and even life threatening and the person may need medical supervision. Dependence leads the patient to ignore all social norms in order to get sufficient funds to satiate his/her needs. These result in many social adjustment problems.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option 1.Immediate adverse effects of drug and alcohol abuse include reckless behavior, vandalism, and violence.
2.Excessive doses of drugs can lead to severe outcomes such as coma, respiratory failure, heart failure, or cerebral hemorrhage.
3.Combining drugs with alcohol often results in overdosing and can be fatal.
4.Warning signs of drug and alcohol abuse in youth include a drop in academic performance, withdrawal, and changes in personal hygiene.
5.Drug and alcohol abuse can have far-reaching implications, including causing mental and financial distress to the user's family and friends.
questions.solution: The immediate adverse effects of drugs and alcohol abuse are manifested in the form of reckless behaviour, vandalism and violence. Excessive doses of drugs may lead to coma and death due to respiratory failure, heart failure or cerebral hemorrhage. A combination of drugs or their intake along with alcohol generally results in overdosing and even deaths. The most common warning signs of drug and alcohol abuse among youth include drop in academic performance, unexplained absence from school/college, lack of interest in personal hygiene, withdrawal, isolation, depression, fatigue, aggressive and rebellious behaviour, deteriorating relationships with family and friends, loss of interest in hobbies, change in sleeping and eating habits, fluctuations in weight, appetite, etc

A combination of drugs or their intake along with alcohol generally results in overdosing and even deaths. The most common warning signs of drug and alcohol abuse among youth include drop in academic performance, unexplained absence from school/college, lack of interest in personal hygiene, withdrawal, isolation, depression, fatigue, aggressive and rebellious behaviour, deteriorating relationships with family and friends, loss of interest in hobbies, change in sleeping and eating habits, fluctuations in weight, appetite, etc

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
The correct sequence of events in the life cycle of Plasmodium is:

A. Parasites reproduce asexually in the liver cells and then burst into the blood.
B. Fertilization and development take place in the mosquito's gut.
C. Sporozoites are injected into the human body through a mosquito bite.
D. Gametocytes are taken up by a female Anopheles mosquito during a blood meal.
E. Parasites reproduce asexually in red blood cells, causing them to rupture and release hemozoin.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Refer: NCERT | Class 12 | Page: 132 | Diagram

The life cycle of Plasmodium starts when an infected female Anopheles mosquito bites a healthy human, injecting the infective stage, sporozoites, into the human body (C).

The sporozoites reach the liver through the blood, where they reproduce asexually in the liver cells, bursting the cells and releasing the parasites into the blood (A).

These parasites then enter the red blood cells (RBCs) and reproduce asexually, causing the RBCs to rupture. The rupture of RBCs is associated with the release of a toxic substance called hemozoin, which is responsible for the chill and high fever (E).

Some of the parasites in the RBCs differentiate into sexual stages called gametocytes. When a female Anopheles mosquito bites the infected person, these gametocytes are taken up along with the blood meal (D).

Inside the mosquito's body, fertilization and further development of the gametes take place in the gut, forming sporozoites which migrate to the salivary glands (B).

The correct sequence of events is C, A, E, D, B.

Answer: (1) C, A, E, D, B

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option
1. Intravenous drug users are at higher risk of acquiring serious infections such as AIDS and Hepatitis B due to sharing infected needles.
2. Both AIDS and Hepatitis B can be transmitted through sexual contact or infected blood.
3. Long-term use of alcohol during adolescence can lead to heavy drinking in adulthood and chronic damage to the nervous system and liver.
4.The use of drugs and alcohol during pregnancy does not affect the fetus.
5. Misuse of anabolic steroids in sports can cause various side effects, including masculinization in females and enlargement of testicle size in males.
questions.solution: Those who take drugs intravenously (direct injection into the vein using a needle and syringe), are much more likely to acquire serious infections like AIDS and Hepatitis B. The viruses, which are responsible for these diseases, are transferred from one person to another by sharing of infected needles and syringes. Both AIDS and Hepatitis B infections are chronic infections and ultimately fatal. Both can be transmitted through sexual contact or infected blood. The use of alcohol during adolescence may also have long-term effects. It could lead to heavy drinking in adulthood. The chronic use of drugs and alcohol damages nervous system and liver (cirrhosis). The use of drugs and alcohol during pregnancy is also known to adversely affect the foetus.

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option
1. The adage "prevention is better than cure" is applicable to preventing substance abuse, including smoking, drugs, and alcohol.
2.Adolescence is a critical period where habits like smoking and drug use are more likely to develop.
3.Identifying and addressing situations that might push adolescents towards substance abuse is crucial for prevention.
4.Parents and teachers play a key role in preventing substance abuse through effective parenting and guidance.
5.Avoiding undue peer pressure and respecting individual choices are important measures in preventing adolescent substance abuse.
questions.solution: The age-old adage of ‘prevention is better than cure’ holds true here also. It is also true that habits such as smoking, taking drug or alcohol are more likely to be taken up at a young age, more during adolescence. Hence, it is best to identify the situations that may push an adolescent towards use of drugs or alcohol, and to take remedial measures well in time. In this regard, the parents and the teachers have a special responsibility. Parenting that combines with high levels of nurturance and consistent discipline, has been associated with lowered risk of substance (alcohol/drugs/tobacco) abuse. Some of the measures mentioned here would be particularly useful for prevention and control of alcohol and drugs abuse among adolescents (i) Avoid undue peer pressure - Every child has his/her own choice and personality, which should be respected and nurtured. A child should not be pushed unduly to perform beyond his/her threshold limits; be it studies, sports or other activities.

B. Artificial passive2. Injection of antiserum
C. Artificial active3. Fighting infection
D. Natural passive4. Induced vaccination
questions.solution:
Natural active immunity occurs when the body fights off an infection on its own, leading to long-term immunity.
Artificial passive immunity is obtained by receiving an injection of antiserum or antibodies to provide immediate but temporary protection.
Artificial active immunity is induced through vaccination, where the immune system is stimulated to produce a response against a pathogen.
Natural passive immunity is transferred from mother to fetus through the placenta, providing the baby with temporary immunity.

questions.q:
Event during plasmodium life cycleSite
A. Asexual reproduction of sporozoites1. Salivary gland of mosquito
B. Haemozoin formation2. Gut of mosquito
C. Fertilization3. RBC of human
D. Storage of sporozoites4. Liver cells of human
questions.solution:
Asexual reproduction of sporozoites: Occurs in the liver cells of humans where sporozoites multiply after initial infection.
Haemozoin formation: Takes place in the RBCs of humans as Plasmodium parasites digest hemoglobin, leading to the release of haemozoin pigment.
Fertilization: Happens in the gut of the mosquito where male and female gametocytes from human blood fuse.
Storage of sporozoites: Sporozoites are stored in the salivary glands of the mosquito, ready to be transmitted to another human host during a bite.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Type of immunoglobulinCharacteristic
A. IgG1. First antibody produced during primary immune response
B. IgA2. Found in mucosal areas like the gut, respiratory tract, and urogenital tract
C. IgM3. Provides long-term immunity; crosses the placenta
D. IgE4. Involved in allergic reactions; binds to mast cells and basophils
questions.solution:
IgG is the most abundant immunoglobulin in the blood and is critical for long-term immunity. It is the only immunoglobulin that can cross the placenta, providing passive immunity to the fetus.
IgA is primarily found in mucosal areas, such as the gut, respiratory tract, and urogenital tract, and in secretions like saliva, tears, and breast milk. It plays a crucial role in mucosal immunity.
IgM is the first antibody produced in response to an infection during the primary immune response. It is also the largest antibody in terms of molecular structure.
IgE is associated with allergic reactions. It binds to receptors on mast cells and basophils, leading to the release of histamine and other mediators during allergic responses.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A patient presents with symptoms of fatigue, weakening, and paralysis of skeletal muscles. Clinical investigations reveal that the patient's own immune system is producing antibodies that attack the neuromuscular junction. Identify the disease and its correct biological categorization.
questions.solution:
The symptoms described (fatigue, weakening, and paralysis of skeletal muscles) and the specific targeting of the neuromuscular junction are characteristic of Myasthenia gravis.

Because the patient's own immune system produces antibodies against their own receptors, it is classified as an autoimmune disorder.

Muscular dystrophy is a genetic disorder that causes progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle, not an autoimmune attack on the neuromuscular junction.

Answer: Myasthenia gravis - Autoimmune disorder

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
(A) Plasmodium, a tiny protozoan, is responsible for malaria.
(B) Rhinoviruses represent a group of bacteria that cause the common cold.
(C) Ascaris, an intestinal parasite, is a helminth that causes ascariasis.
(D) Microsporum and Trichophyton are protozoans responsible for ringworm.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct because malaria is caused by Plasmodium, which is a protozoan.

Statement (B) is incorrect because rhinoviruses are a group of viruses, not bacteria.

Statement (C) is correct because Ascaris is a common roundworm (helminth) that causes ascariasis.

Statement (D) is incorrect because Microsporum and Trichophyton are fungi, not protozoans, that cause ringworm.

Therefore, exactly two statements ((A) and (C)) are correct.

Answer: Two

Read the following statements regarding the barriers of innate immunity:

(A) Mucus coating of the epithelium lining the respiratory tract is a physiological barrier.
(B) Acid in the stomach and saliva in the mouth are examples of physical barriers.
(C) Natural killer cells in the blood are a type of lymphocyte that act as cellular barriers.
(D) Interferons are proteins secreted by bacteria-infected cells to protect non-infected cells.

How many of the given statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is incorrect because the mucus coating of the epithelium lining the respiratory, gastrointestinal, and urogenital tracts is a physical barrier, not a physiological barrier.

Statement (B) is incorrect because acid in the stomach, saliva in the mouth, and tears from the eyes are physiological barriers, not physical barriers.

Statement (C) is correct as Natural killer cells are a type of lymphocyte present in the blood that function as cellular barriers of innate immunity.

Statement (D) is incorrect because interferons are cytokine barriers secreted specifically by virus-infected cells, not bacteria-infected cells.

Therefore, only one statement (C) is correct.

Answer: Only one

questions.q: Drug 'X' is chemically diacetylmorphine, which is synthesized by the acetylation of an extract obtained from a specific plant. Identify the correct plant source of this extract and the specific locations of the receptors for drug 'X' in the human body.
options: Leaves of Cannabis sativa; Receptors are present in the cardiovascular system
Latex of Papaver somniferum; Receptors are present in the cardiovascular system
Latex of Papaver somniferum; Receptors are present in the central nervous system and gastrointestinal tract
Erythroxylum coca; Receptors are present in the central nervous system
questions.solution:
Drug 'X', which is chemically diacetylmorphine, is commonly known as heroin. It is synthesized by the acetylation of morphine.

Morphine is extracted from the latex of the poppy plant, Papaver somniferum.

Heroin binds to specific opioid receptors, which are located in the central nervous system (CNS) and the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. Cannabinoids interact with receptors mainly in the brain and affect the cardiovascular system, while cocaine is obtained from Erythroxylum coca.

Answer: Latex of Papaver somniferum; Receptors are present in the central nervous system and gastrointestinal tract

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
A person suffering from a common cold caused by a rhinovirus experiences excessive mucus production in the respiratory tract. Meanwhile, the virus-infected cells of the respiratory epithelium secrete specific protective proteins to prevent the infection of adjacent healthy cells.

Which two types of innate immunity barriers are respectively represented by the mucus coating and the protective proteins mentioned in the scenario?
questions.solution:
The excessive mucus production in the respiratory tract acts as a physical barrier. According to NCERT, the mucus coating of the epithelium lining the respiratory, gastrointestinal, and urogenital tracts helps in trapping microbes entering our body, forming a physical barrier of innate immunity.

The specific protective proteins secreted by virus-infected cells are interferons. Interferons protect non-infected cells from further viral infection and constitute the cytokine barrier of innate immunity.

Therefore, the mucus coating and the protective proteins represent the physical barrier and the cytokine barrier, respectively.

Answer: Physical barrier and Cytokine barrier

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The thymus is quite large at the time of birth but keeps reducing in size with age, becoming very small by puberty.
Reason (R): It is a secondary lymphoid organ that loses its function once the acquired immune system is fully developed.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
The Assertion is a correct statement. According to NCERT, the thymus is quite large at the time of birth but keeps reducing in size with age and by the time puberty is attained it reduces to a very small size.

The Reason is an incorrect statement. The thymus is a primary lymphoid organ, not a secondary lymphoid organ. Primary lymphoid organs (bone marrow and thymus) are the sites where immature lymphocytes differentiate into antigen-sensitive lymphocytes.

Therefore, Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

The medical history reveals that at higher doses, the individual experiences hallucinations. The drug responsible for these symptoms is obtained from a plant native to South America. Identify the plant source and the most common route of administration for this drug.
questions.solution:
The symptoms described (euphoria, increased energy, and hallucinations at high doses) are characteristic of cocaine intoxication.

Cocaine is an alkaloid obtained from the coca plant Erythroxylum coca, which is native to South America.

According to NCERT, cocaine, commonly called coke or crack, is usually snorted.

Papaver somniferum yields opioids like heroin, which act as depressants rather than stimulants. Cannabis sativa yields cannabinoids, which are known for their effects on the cardiovascular system and are not the primary cause of the strong euphoria and energy described here. While heroin is commonly injected intravenously, cocaine is primarily snorted.

Answer: Erythroxylum coca, Snorting

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In malaria, the characteristic chills and high fever recurring every 3 to 4 days are experienced immediately after the infective sporozoites multiply in and burst the liver cells.

Reason (R): The rupture of infected red blood cells (RBCs) is associated with the release of a toxic substance, hemozoin, which is responsible for the chill and high fever.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is false because the initial multiplication of sporozoites in the liver cells and their subsequent bursting does not cause the characteristic chills and fever. The fever and chills occur later, during the erythrocytic phase when red blood cells are infected and ruptured.

Reason (R) is true because the rupture of infected red blood cells (RBCs) releases a toxic substance called hemozoin, which is responsible for the recurring chills and high fever every 3 to 4 days.

Therefore, Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Innate immunity consists of different types of barriers that prevent the entry of foreign agents into our body. Which of the following is an incorrectly matched pair of an innate immunity barrier and its example?
questions.solution:
Saliva in the mouth, tears from the eyes, and acid in the stomach are examples of physiological barriers that prevent microbial growth. Therefore, matching saliva in the mouth with 'Physical barrier' is incorrect.

Physical barriers include the skin on our body and the mucus coating of the epithelium lining the respiratory, gastrointestinal, and urogenital tracts.

Polymorpho-nuclear leukocytes (PMNL-neutrophils) act as cellular barriers by phagocytosing and destroying microbes.

Interferons act as cytokine barriers, which are secreted by virus-infected cells to protect non-infected cells from further viral infections.

Answer: Saliva in mouth $-$ Physical barrier

Gout is the inflammation of joints due to the accumulation of uric acid crystals.

Gout is correctly described as the inflammation of joints due to the accumulation of uric acid crystals.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the human immune system:
(A) B-lymphocytes produce an army of proteins called antibodies in response to pathogens.
(B) T-cells themselves secrete antibodies to neutralize the pathogens in the blood.
(C) Colostrum secreted by the mother during the initial days of lactation provides active immunity to the newborn.
(D) Interferons are secreted by virus-infected cells to protect non-infected cells.

How many of the given statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct as B-lymphocytes produce an army of proteins called antibodies in our blood to fight pathogens.

Statement (B) is incorrect because T-cells themselves do not secrete antibodies, but they help B-cells to produce them.

Statement (C) is incorrect because colostrum contains pre-formed antibodies (IgA) and provides natural passive immunity to the newborn, not active immunity.

Statement (D) is correct as virus-infected cells secrete proteins called interferons which protect non-infected cells from further viral infection.

Therefore, exactly two statements, (A) and (D), are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.solution:

The rupture of human red blood cells (RBCs) is associated with the release of a toxic substance, hemozoin, which is responsible for the chill and high fever (A-III).

The infective stage, sporozoites, are stored in the salivary glands of the female Anopheles mosquito until she bites a human (B-II).

Fertilisation and further development of the parasite take place in the mosquito's gut (C-I).

When sporozoites enter the human body, they first reach the liver cells through blood and undergo initial multiplication (D-IV).

Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV.

Answer: A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV

questions.solution:
The drugs that bind to specific receptors present in our central nervous system and gastrointestinal tract are opioids.

Morphine is an example of an opioid. It is a very effective sedative and painkiller, and is very useful in patients who have undergone surgery.

Marijuana contains cannabinoids, whose receptors are principally present in the brain. Cocaine is a coca alkaloid that interferes with dopamine transport. Hallucinations are typically caused by excessive dosage of cocaine or by drugs like LSD, not primarily by morphine.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Organs transplanted from any source cannot be simply accepted by the patient's body, and immunosuppressants are often required even after successful tissue matching.
Reason (R): The cell-mediated immune response, mediated by T-lymphocytes, is able to differentiate between 'self' and 'non-self' and is responsible for graft rejection.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true. Grafts or organs transplanted from any source cannot be accepted because the body's immune system will reject them. Even after tissue and blood group matching, patients often need to take immunosuppressants for life.

Reason (R) is also true and correctly explains the Assertion. The body's immune system is capable of differentiating between 'self' and 'non-self'. The cell-mediated immune response (CMI), which is mediated by T-lymphocytes, is primarily responsible for recognizing the transplanted organ as 'non-self' and causing graft rejection. Thus, immunosuppressants are required to suppress this T-cell mediated response.

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is a correct statement. According to NCERT, virus-infected cells secrete specific proteins called interferons, which protect adjacent non-infected cells from further viral infection.

Reason (R) is an incorrect statement. While it is true that interferons constitute the cytokine barriers, these barriers are one of the four types of innate immunity (present at birth and non-specific), not acquired immunity. Acquired immunity is pathogen-specific and characterised by memory.

Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A patient presents to a clinic with sustained high fever ($39^{\circ}\text{C}$ to $40^{\circ}\text{C}$), weakness, stomach pain, constipation, headache, and loss of appetite. Identify the biological category of the causative agent and the standard diagnostic test used to confirm this disease.
questions.solution:
The clinical symptoms described (sustained high fever of $39^{\circ}\text{C}$ to $40^{\circ}\text{C}$, weakness, stomach pain, constipation, headache, and loss of appetite) are the classic symptoms of Typhoid fever.

Typhoid is caused by the pathogenic bacterium Salmonella typhi.

The standard confirmatory diagnostic test for Typhoid is the Widal test.

Therefore, the causative agent belongs to the category of Bacteria, and the correct test is the Widal test. ELISA is widely used for viral infections like HIV, while blood smears are typically used for protozoan infections like Malaria.

Answer: Bacteria and Widal test

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the lymphoid organs in the human body:

(A) MALT constitutes about 50 percent of the lymphoid tissue in the human body.
(B) MALT is located within the lining of major tracts like respiratory, digestive and urogenital tracts.
(C) Bone marrow and thymus are secondary lymphoid organs where lymphocytes interact with antigens.
(D) The spleen is a large bean-shaped organ that mainly contains lymphocytes and phagocytes, acting as a filter of the blood.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct as Mucosa-Associated Lymphoid Tissue (MALT) constitutes about 50 percent of the lymphoid tissue in the human body.

Statement (B) is correct as MALT is located within the lining of the major tracts (respiratory, digestive and urogenital tracts).

Statement (C) is incorrect because bone marrow and thymus are primary lymphoid organs where immature lymphocytes differentiate into antigen-sensitive lymphocytes. Secondary lymphoid organs (like spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils) are the sites where lymphocytes actually interact with antigens.

Statement (D) is correct as the spleen is a large bean-shaped organ containing lymphocytes and phagocytes, and it acts as a filter of the blood by trapping blood-borne microorganisms.

Therefore, exactly three statements ((A), (B), and (D)) are correct.

Answer: Three

List-IList-II
A. Benign tumorI. Property of normal cells that inhibits uncontrolled growth
B. Malignant tumorII. Mass of proliferating neoplastic cells that invade tissues
C. MetastasisIII. Remains confined to original location
D. Contact inhibitionIV. Spread of tumor cells to distant sites

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Benign tumors normally remain confined to their original location and do not spread, causing little damage (A matches III).

Malignant tumors are masses of proliferating cells called neoplastic cells that grow rapidly and invade surrounding normal tissues (B matches II).

Metastasis is the most feared property of malignant tumors, where tumor cells spread to distant sites via the bloodstream to form new tumors (C matches IV).

Contact inhibition is a property of normal cells that inhibits their uncontrolled growth upon contact with other cells (D matches I).

Thus, the correct matching is A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I.

Answer: A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
(A) Primary lymphoid organs provide the sites for interaction of lymphocytes with the antigen.
(B) Thymus is quite large at the time of birth but keeps reducing in size with age.
(C) Peyer's patches of small intestine and appendix are secondary lymphoid organs.
(D) MALT constitutes about 20 percent of the lymphoid tissue in the human body.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is incorrect because secondary lymphoid organs (not primary) provide the sites for interaction of lymphocytes with the antigen. Primary lymphoid organs (bone marrow and thymus) are where immature lymphocytes differentiate into antigen-sensitive lymphocytes.

Statement (B) is correct. The thymus is quite large at the time of birth but keeps reducing in size with age, and by the time puberty is attained it reduces to a very small size.

Statement (C) is correct. Spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, Peyer's patches of small intestine and appendix are secondary lymphoid organs.

Statement (D) is incorrect because MALT constitutes about 50 percent (not 20 percent) of the lymphoid tissue in the human body.

Thus, exactly two statements, (B) and (C), are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Read the following statements regarding HIV/AIDS and its prevention, and choose the incorrect statement.
options: HIV can be transmitted by mere touch or physical contact, which NACO campaigns aim to prevent.
HIV enters T-helper lymphocytes, replicates, and causes a progressive decrease in their count.
NACO and other non-governmental organisations educate people to prevent infection because AIDS has no cure.
Macrophages continue to produce the virus and act like an HIV factory while surviving the infection.
questions.solution:
The statement in option 1 is incorrect. HIV/AIDS is not spread by mere touch or physical contact; it spreads only through body fluids. Therefore, campaigns by NACO (National AIDS Control Organisation) focus on safe blood transfusions, use of disposable needles, and safe sex, rather than preventing physical contact.

The statement in option 2 is correct. After entering the body, HIV enters T-helper lymphocytes, replicates, and produces progeny viruses, leading to a progressive decrease in their count and weakening the immune system.

The statement in option 3 is correct. Since AIDS has no cure, prevention is the best option. NACO and NGOs educate people to raise awareness.

The statement in option 4 is correct. The virus enters macrophages where its RNA genome replicates to form viral DNA, which directs the infected cells to produce virus particles. The macrophage survives and continues to act like an HIV factory.

Answer: HIV can be transmitted by mere touch or physical contact, which NACO campaigns aim to prevent.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
(A) Innate immunity is a pathogen-specific type of defence present at the time of birth.
(B) Skin on our body is the main physical barrier which prevents entry of the micro-organisms.
(C) Saliva in the mouth and tears from eyes are cellular barriers of innate immunity.
(D) Virus-infected cells secrete proteins called interferons which form cytokine barriers.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is incorrect because innate immunity is a non-specific type of defence, whereas acquired immunity is pathogen-specific.

Statement (B) is correct as skin is the main physical barrier preventing the entry of micro-organisms.

Statement (C) is incorrect because saliva in the mouth and tears from eyes are physiological barriers, not cellular barriers. Cellular barriers include certain types of leukocytes like PMNL-neutrophils and monocytes.

Statement (D) is correct as virus-infected cells secrete interferons which protect non-infected cells from further viral infection, constituting the cytokine barrier.

Therefore, exactly two statements are correct.

Answer: Only two

Match List-I with List-II regarding drug-yielding plants and their physiological effects.

List-I (Plant)List-II (Effect/Property)
(A) Papaver somniferum(I) Affects cardiovascular system of the body

(D) Datura(IV) Interferes with the transport of dopamine

questions.solution:
Papaver somniferum yields opioids (such as heroin), which bind to specific opioid receptors in the central nervous system and gastrointestinal tract, acting as a depressant that slows down body functions.

Cannabis sativa yields cannabinoids, which are known for their effects on the cardiovascular system of the body.

Datura contains alkaloids that possess hallucinogenic properties.

Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A patient infected with Plasmodium experiences recurring episodes of chills and high fever every 3 to 4 days. Which cellular event is directly responsible for these symptoms, and what is the subsequent developmental process of the parasite that occurs within the same host?
options: Rupture of red blood cells releasing hemozoin; Differentiation into gametocytes
Rupture of liver cells releasing parasites; Differentiation into gametocytes
Rupture of red blood cells releasing hemozoin; Fertilisation of gametes
Release of sporozoites into the blood; Initial multiplication in liver cells
questions.solution:
The recurring chills and high fever in malaria are caused by the rupture of infected red blood cells (RBCs), which releases a toxic substance called hemozoin into the bloodstream.

Following the asexual reproduction and rupture of RBCs, some of the parasites differentiate into the sexual stages known as gametocytes. This differentiation occurs within the human red blood cells (the same host).

Fertilisation and further development of these gametes do not occur in the human host; instead, they take place in the gut of the female Anopheles mosquito after she takes a blood meal.

Therefore, the correct sequence of events in the human host is the rupture of RBCs releasing hemozoin, followed by the differentiation into gametocytes.

Answer: Rupture of red blood cells releasing hemozoin; Differentiation into gametocytes

questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
(A) MRI uses ionizing radiations and strong magnetic fields to detect pathological changes.
(B) Computed tomography uses X-rays to generate a three-dimensional image of the internal organs.
(C) UV rays are non-ionizing radiations that cause DNA damage leading to neoplastic transformation.
(D) Cellular oncogenes (c-onc) present in normal cells can lead to oncogenic transformation when activated.
(E) Antibodies against cancer-specific antigens are used for the detection of certain cancers.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is incorrect because MRI uses strong magnetic fields and non-ionizing radiations (not ionizing radiations) to accurately detect pathological and physiological changes in living tissue.

Statement (B) is correct as Computed tomography (CT) uses X-rays to generate a 3-D image of the internals of an object.

Statement (C) is correct because non-ionizing radiations like UV cause DNA damage leading to neoplastic transformation.

Statement (D) is correct as cellular oncogenes (c-onc) or proto-oncogenes in normal cells can lead to oncogenic transformation when activated under certain conditions.

Statement (E) is correct as antibodies against cancer-specific antigens are used for cancer detection.

Therefore, exactly four statements are correct.

Answer: Four

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Rheumatoid arthritis is considered an autoimmune disease.
Reason (R): In certain conditions, the body's immune system loses the ability to distinguish 'self' cells from 'non-self' and attacks its own cells.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true. According to NCERT, rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic inflammatory disorder that is classified as an auto-immune disease.

Reason (R) is true and correctly explains the assertion. Auto-immunity occurs when the immune system, due to genetic or other unknown reasons, loses the ability to distinguish between 'self' and 'non-self' cells, leading to an immune response against the body's own tissues. Rheumatoid arthritis is a direct consequence of this loss of self-tolerance, making the reason the correct explanation for the assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A patient is brought to a clinic exhibiting a strong sense of euphoria and increased energy. The clinical report notes that an excessive dosage of the abused substance has also induced hallucinations. Identify the source plant of this substance and its primary mechanism of action.
options: Cannabis sativa - Known for its effects on the cardiovascular system
Erythroxylum coca - Interferes with the transport of the neurotransmitter dopamine
Papaver somniferum - Acts as a depressant and slows down body functions
Atropa belladonna - Interferes with the transport of the neurotransmitter dopamine
questions.solution:
The symptoms described (a sense of euphoria, increased energy, and hallucinations upon excessive dosage) are characteristic of cocaine.

According to NCERT, cocaine (coca alkaloid) is obtained from the coca plant Erythroxylum coca.

Its primary mechanism of action is interfering with the transport of the neurotransmitter dopamine.

Cannabis sativa yields cannabinoids which affect the cardiovascular system. Papaver somniferum is the source of opioids (like morphine and heroin) which act as depressants. While Atropa belladonna has hallucinogenic properties, it is not the source of cocaine and does not primarily act by interfering with dopamine transport.

Answer: Erythroxylum coca - Interferes with the transport of the neurotransmitter dopamine

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Interferons form the cytokine barrier of innate immunity to protect non-infected cells from further viral infection.

Reason (R): Interferons are specialized antibodies secreted by virus-infected cells.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because interferons are proteins secreted by virus-infected cells that protect adjacent non-infected cells from further viral infection. They constitute the cytokine barrier of innate immunity.

Reason (R) is not correct because interferons are proteins, not antibodies. Antibodies are produced by B-lymphocytes in response to pathogens and form a part of acquired immunity, whereas interferons are part of innate immunity.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.solution:

Assertion (A): Cancer cells continue to divide and form masses of cells called tumors.
Reason (R): Cancer cells appear to have lost the property of contact inhibition.

options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
Normal cells exhibit a property called contact inhibition, which prevents their uncontrolled growth when they come in contact with other cells.

Cancer cells lose this property of contact inhibition. As a direct result of this loss, they continue to divide uncontrollably, leading to the formation of masses of cells known as tumors.

Therefore, both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the cellular mechanism behind the Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the life cycle of Plasmodium inside the female Anopheles mosquito:

Statement I: The mosquito takes up sporozoites along with the human blood meal.
Statement II: Fertilization and subsequent development of the parasite take place in the mosquito's gut.
Statement III: The mature infective stages escape from the gut and migrate to the mosquito's salivary glands.
Statement IV: Gametocytes are originally formed inside the mosquito's intestine immediately after the blood meal.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is incorrect because the female Anopheles mosquito takes up gametocytes (sexual stages), not sporozoites, along with the human blood meal.

Statement II is correct as fertilization and further development of the Plasmodium parasite occur in the mosquito's gut.

Statement III is correct because the mature infective stages (sporozoites) escape from the gut and migrate to the mosquito's salivary glands, where they are stored.

Statement IV is incorrect because gametocytes are originally formed in the red blood cells (RBCs) of the human host, not in the mosquito's intestine.

Thus, exactly two statements (II and III) are correct.

Answer: Two

Cells of malignant tumors actively damage surrounding normal tissues by ____(A)____ and exhibit the most feared property called ____(B)____.
options: (A) remaining confined to their location, (B) metastasis
(A) competing for vital nutrients, (B) contact inhibition
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, cells of malignant tumors grow very rapidly, invading and damaging the surrounding normal tissues. As these cells actively divide and grow, they starve the normal cells by competing for vital nutrients (Blank A).

Cells sloughed from such tumors reach distant sites through blood and start a new tumor there. This property is called metastasis (Blank B), which is the most feared property of malignant tumors. Contact inhibition is a property of normal cells, not malignant ones.

Answer: (A) competing for vital nutrients, (B) metastasis

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A patient undergoes a successful kidney transplant but is prescribed immunosuppressants for the rest of their life to prevent graft rejection. Which specific type of immune response is primarily responsible for this rejection, and to which broader category of immunity does it belong?
questions.solution:
Graft rejection in organ transplantation is primarily mediated by T-lymphocytes, which are responsible for the cell-mediated immune response (CMI).

Cell-mediated immunity is a highly specific immune response that develops during an individual's lifetime and is characterised by immunological memory. Therefore, it is a sub-type of acquired immunity, not innate immunity.

Humoral immunity, mediated by B-lymphocytes (antibodies), is not the primary cause of graft rejection.

Answer: Cell-mediated immunity; Acquired immunity

questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true because malignant tumors have cells that slough off and reach distant sites through blood, forming new tumors wherever they lodge. This property, called metastasis, is the most feared property of cancer.

Reason (R) is also true because cells of malignant tumors grow rapidly, invading and damaging surrounding normal tissues. As these cells actively divide and grow, they also starve the normal cells by competing for vital nutrients.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A developing foetus receives some antibodies from the mother through the placenta during pregnancy. After birth, the newborn infant receives antibodies from the mother through colostrum. Identify the primary antibody types involved in the first and second cases respectively, and the specific type of immunity they represent.
questions.solution:
The foetus receives IgG antibodies from the mother through the placenta, which is the only antibody class capable of crossing the placental barrier.

After birth, the infant receives IgA antibodies, which are abundantly present in colostrum (the yellowish fluid secreted during the initial days of lactation).

In both cases, pre-formed antibodies are directly transferred from the mother to the child to provide immediate protection. This transfer of ready-made antibodies under natural physiological conditions is an example of natural passive immunity. It is not active immunity because the infant's own immune system is not producing these antibodies, and it is not artificial because no medical intervention (like an injection) is involved.

Answer: IgG, IgA, Natural passive immunity

questions.solution:
The spread of a tumor from its primary site (liver) to distant organs (lungs) indicates that the tumor is not confined to its original location. Therefore, it is a malignant tumor.

questions.q: After maturation, lymphocytes migrate to certain organs which provide the sites for interaction of lymphocytes with the antigen, which then proliferate to become effector cells. Identify the organ that performs this function from the given options.
questions.solution:
Primary lymphoid organs (bone marrow and thymus) are the sites where immature lymphocytes differentiate into antigen-sensitive lymphocytes.

After maturation, lymphocytes migrate to secondary lymphoid organs, which provide the sites for interaction of lymphocytes with the antigen, which then proliferate to become effector cells.

Spleen is a secondary lymphoid organ. Thymus and bone marrow are primary lymphoid organs, while the thyroid is an endocrine gland.

Answer: Spleen

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Ringworm is a fungal disease that commonly affects skin folds such as those in the groin or between the toes.
Reason (R): Fungi belonging to genera like Microsporum and Epidermophyton require heat and moisture to thrive and grow.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because ringworm is a common fungal infection in humans, and it frequently occurs in areas where skin folds are present, such as the groin or between the toes.

Reason (R) is correct because fungi such as Microsporum, Trichophyton, and Epidermophyton thrive in environments that provide heat and moisture.

The heat and moisture found in skin folds create the ideal conditions for these fungi to grow, which perfectly explains why ringworm commonly affects these specific areas. Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following characteristics of a lymphoid organ:
(i) It is a large bean-shaped organ.
(ii) It mainly contains lymphocytes and phagocytes.
(iii) It acts as a filter of the blood by trapping blood-borne microorganisms.

Identify the organ based on the above description.
questions.solution:
The spleen is a large bean-shaped secondary lymphoid organ that mainly contains lymphocytes and phagocytes. It acts as a filter of the blood by trapping blood-borne microorganisms.

Lymph nodes are small solid structures that trap microorganisms present in the lymph and tissue fluid, not the blood.

Thymus is a lobed primary lymphoid organ located near the heart.

Tonsils are secondary lymphoid organs but do not fit the description of a large bean-shaped blood filter.

Answer: Spleen

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Humoral immunity is mediated by which of the following ?
questions.solution: Antibody mediated immune system or humoral immunity consists of antibodies (specialised proteins produced in the body in response to antigen) that circulate in the body fluids like blood plasma and lymph. B-lymphocytes (B-cells) produce antibodies that regulate humoral immunity. T-lymphocytes themselves do not secrete antibodies but help B-lymphocytes produce them. Humoral immunity provides defence against most extracellular bacterial pathogens and viruses that infect through respiratory and intestinal tract.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Assertion : Cancer cells are virtually immortal until the body in which they reside dies.
Reason : Cancer is caused by damage to genes regulating the cell division cycle.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Cancer is a growth disorder of cells. It starts when an apparently normal cell begins to grow in an uncontrolled and invasive way. The result is a cluster of cells, called a tumor, that constantly expands in size. Cells that leave the tumour, spread throughout the body, forming new tumours at distant sites. This is called metastasis. Cancer is a gene disorder of somatic tissue, in which damaged genes fail to properly control cell proliferation. A series of several mutations to certain classes of genes is usually required before a normal cell will transform into a cancer cell. All cancers are characterised by unrestrained growth and division. Cell division never stops in a cancerous cells. Cancer cells are virtually immortal-until the body in which they reside dies.

questions.solution: Inside the red blood cells, oval-shaped merozoites stop proceeding with erythrocytic cycle to increase in size and become rounded gametocytes. Male gametocytes or microgametocytes are smaller and contain a large diffused nucleus. Female gametocytes (or mega gametocytes) are larger with a small compact peripheral nucleus. These do not divide but remain as intracellular parasites within their host's blood corpuscles, until they either die or are ingested by the vectors. They give rise to gametes in insects.

questions.solution: A healthy person acquires infection when a female Anopheles mosquito, containing infective stages of parasite (sporozoites) in its salivary glands, bites him for sucking his blood. The mosquito punctures the host's skin by its proboscis and first introduces some saliva into blood stream. Along with saliva, thousands of sporozoites contained therein are also inoculated. Sporozoites represent the infective forms of parasite. These are small spindle-shaped, slightly curved or sickleshaped, and uninucleate organisms, measuring $11-12 \mu \mathrm{m}$ in length and $0.5-1 \mu \mathrm{m}$ in width. After infection sporozoites enter liver cells here after a few divisions, micrometacryptomerozoites are formed that enter RBC's and gametocytes are formed here in $R B C^{\prime} s$.

If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: A small, glandular, blind pouch of lymphatic tissue, the bursa lies on the dorsal side of the cloaca. It is lined with endoderm, and opens into the proctodaeum. In a young bird, bursa fabricii forms lymphocytes, and probably it produces antibodies and protects against local infection, but it atrophies in the adult before sexual maturity. It is also called cloacal thymus, because like thymus, it secretes lymphocytes. Thus it is not related with flight adaptation, rather it helps in immunity.

questions.q: Smoking addiction is harmful because it produces polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, which cause
questions.solution:
Cancer is caused by cells dividing repeatedly out of control. They cease to respond to the normal signals around them and form unspecialised masses of cells called tumours. Lung cancer usually starts in the epithelium of the bronchioles, so-called bronchial carcinoma. It then usually spreads throughout the lungs. It is caused almost exclusively by smoking.
Tobacco smoke contains chemicals responsible for lung cancer. The most important of these are polycyclic hydrocarbons which are converted in the body to carcinogens.
Besides, carbon monoxide combines with haemoglobin and reduces oxygen transport by about $15 \%$ in smokers and nicotine increases blood pressure, heart rate and constriction of blood vessels.

questions.solution: Rabies (hydrophobia) is an acute viral disease of the central nervous system that affects all warmblooded animals and is usually transmitted to humans by a bite from an infected dog. Symptoms appear after an incubation period ranging from 10 days to over a year and include malaise, fever, difficulty in breathing, salivation, periods of intense excitement, and painful muscle spasms of the throat induced by swallowing. questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Assertion : Antigen can be easily recognized because it has antigenic determinants.
Reason : The recognition ability is innate.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Antigen is any substance that may be specifically bound by an antibody molecule. The antigens are mostly proteins, but can be polysaccharides, glycoproteins or other types of conjugated proteins, nucleic acid or such chemicals. Each antigen has many antigenic determinants (called epitopes) of the antigen. As each antibody binds with 2 or more such determinants, the one antigen can bind with many antibodies. In order to generate antibodies specific for small molecules, the latter are attached to a larger molecule before immunization. The number of different antigens recognized by lymphocytes in the body is extremely large. The recognition ability is innate and develops without exposure to the antigen. Stem cells differentiate into many million different \(\mathrm{T}\) and \(\mathrm{B}\) lymphocytes, each with the ability to respond to a particular antigen. When the antigen first enters the body, it can bind directly to the appropriate receptors on B cells. However, a full antibody response requires that the B cells contact helper \(T\) cells. In the case of \(T\) cells, the antigen is taken up by an antigen-presenting cells and partially digested. A peptide fragment of it is presented to the appropriate receptors on \(\mathrm{T}\) cells. In either case, the cells are stimulated to divide, forming clones of cells that respond to this antigen.

questions.q: When children play bare footed in pools of dirty water and flood water, they may suffer from disease like
options: guinea worm infection, elephantiasis and amoebic dysentery.
questions.solution:
Leptospirosis (also known as Weil's disease, canicola fever, canefield fever, nanukayami fever or 7-day fever) is a bacterial zoonotic disease caused by spirochaetes of the genus Leptospira that affects humans and a wide range of animals, including mammals, birds, amphibians, and reptiles. It was first described by Adolf Weil in 1886 when he reported an "acute infectious disease with enlargement of spleen, jaundice and nephritis.Humans become infected through contact with water, food, or soil containing urine from these infected animals. This may happen by swallowing contaminated food or water or through skin contact. Leptospirosis is common among watersport enthusiasts in certain areas as prolonged immersion in water is known to promote the entry of the bacteria.
Schistosomiasis or bilharzia is al so called snail fever or swimmer's itch. Schistosomiasis is a lifethreatening parasitic disease caused by a worm that lives in a host snail. Humans can become infected when they come in contact with water in ponds and rivers where the snail lives. The pathology is mostly caused by the large number of eggs becoming stuck in various body parts, in particular the liver (causing liver enlargement and malfunction) and the kidneys (causing kidney damage, detectable by blood in the urine).

questions.solution: Cancer is a growth disorder of cells. It starts when an apparently normal cell begins to grow in an uncontrolled and invasive way. The result is a cluster of cells, called a tumor, that constantly expands in size. Cells that leave the tumor and spread throughout the body, forming new tumors at distant sites, are called metastases. Cancer is a gene disorder of somatic tissue, in which damaged genes fail to properly control cell proliferation. The cell division cycle is regulated by a sophisticated group of proteins. Cancer results from the mutation of the genes encoding these proteins. More than one mutation is necessary for carcinogenesis. In fact, a series of several mutations to certain classes of genes is usually required before a normal cell will transform into a cancer cell. Only mutations in those certain types of genes which play vital roles in cell division, cell death, and DNA repair will cause a cell to lose control of its proliferation. Cancer can be caused by chemicals that mutate DNA or in some instances by viruses that circumvent the cell's normal proliferation controls. Whatever the immediate cause, however, all cancers are characterized by unrestrained growth and division. Cell division never stops in a cancerous line of cells. Cancer cells are virtually immortaluntil the body in which they reside dies.

questions.solution:
An analgesic is any member of the diverse group of drugs used to relieve pain and to achieve analgesia. Analgesic drugs act in various ways on the peripheral and central nervous system; they include paracetamol (acetaminophen), the nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) such as the salicylates, narcotic drugs such as morphine, synthetic drugs with narcotic properties such as tramadol, and various others. LSD and marijuana are used as hallucinogens. Hallucinogens are natural and synthetic (synthesized) substances that, when ingested (taken into the body), significantly alter one's state of consciousness. Hallucinogenic compounds often cause people to see (or think they see) random colours, patterns, events, and objects that do not exist. These substances are sometimes called "pyschedelic," or "mindexpanding" drugs.
Marijuana and hashish, two substances derived from the hemp plant (Cannabis sativa), are also considered natural hallucinogens. Marijuana (also called grass, pot, tea, weed, or reefer), a green herb from the flower of the hemp plant, is considered a mild hallucinogen. Hashish is marijuana in a more potent, concentrated form. Both drugs are usually smoked. Their effects include a feeling of relaxation, faster heart rate, the sensation that time is passing more slowly, and a greater sense of hearing, taste, touch, and smell. LSD (Lysergic Acid Diethylamide) is the most common hallucinogen and one of the most potent mood-changing chemicals. It is manufactured from lysergic acid, found in a fungus that grows on rye and other grains. LSD users may experience flashbacks of visions they had when on the drug. Some LSD users suffer organic brain damage, which results in impaired memory and attention span, confusion, and difficulty in thinking.

Assertion : Interferons are a type of antibodies produced by body cells infected by bacteria. 
Reason : Interferons stimulate inflammation at the site of injury.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution:
Interferons are not antibodies. These are natural proteins produced by the cells of the immune systems of most animals in response to challenges by foreign agents such as viruses, bacteria, parasites and tumor cells. Interferons belong to the large class of glycoproteins known as cytokines. In human body there are three types of interferon $-\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$.
Interferon alpha and beta are produced by many cell types, including T-cells and B-cells and are important component of the antiviral response. They stimulate both macrophages and NK (Natural Killer) cells. They both are also active against tumors. Inflammation is the first response to infection and injury and is critical to body defence. Basically, the inflammatory response is an attempt by the body to restore and maintain homeostasis after injury. Inflammation is the influx of fluid and cells that results in redness, swelling, heat, and pain at the infection site.

questions.solution: In alcoholic person, some part of alcohol is changed into acetaldehyde, which stimulates the formation of fat. This fat is deposited over the wall of arteries and also accumulates in liver cells. Due to which liver gets failed and there is very little regulation of carbohydrate, protein and fat metabolism. This disorder is known as fatty liver syndrome. Later on, the liver gets turned into solid, hard, fibrous organ causing liver cirrhosis.

questions.solution:
Alcoholism is a chronic, often progressive disease in which a person craves alcohol and drinks despite repeated alcohol related problems. It involves a physical dependence on alcohol. It may lead to liver cirrhosis. Cirrhosis is build up of scar tissue that changes the structure of the liver and blocks blood flow.
Cirrhosis can cause varicose veins, which can rupture and potentially triggering internal bleeding.

questions.solution: Thymus gland is found in the upper part of thorax near the heart. It is a bilobed pinkish gland. At the time of birth, it is a prominent gland but in the adult it gradually atrophies. This gland secretes thymosin hormone, thymic humoral factor, thymic factor and thymopoietin.
